subject: SOC 2 dependency mapping & subprocessor evidence request (Nimbus Retail)
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@NimbusRetail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@NimbusRetail.com
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: dependency mapping + cloud subservice details for SOC 2 review

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. For Nimbus's annual SOC 2 update we need to validate third-party coverage for a few controls tied to data residency and key management. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering that Nimbus currently uses?

- Do you consume an AWS SOC report for your infrastructure? If so, do you accept AWS as a carve-out subservice for the scope of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II?
- If you rely on other cloud providers (GCP, Azure) for any pockets of processing, please list them and provide the relevant SOC/SIG artifact names or excerpts.
- A current subprocessor registry (CSV) and an indication which subprocessors were in-scope for the 2025 SOC 2 audit (Type II).
- If Redwood cannot provide a full covered-service bridge letter, can you provide an attestation of shared responsibility mapping for control families (e.g., CC6: system operations, CC7: logical access) so we can present to our auditors?

Appreciate any artifacts you can share. If it helps, a short matrix showing Redwood control -> subservice (provider) -> supporting artifact is ideal. We have a compressed timeline and would like the materials by 2026-08-04.

Best,
Elena
Security Assurance Manager
Nimbus Retail

Attachment: nimbus-request-internal-checklist.xlsx (ref)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@NimbusRetail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dependency mapping + cloud subservice details for SOC 2 review

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can provide: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II 2025 report, an extract of the AWS/OCI/GCP SOC artifacts we consume, and a subprocessor registry highlighting which vendors were in-scope during the 2025 audit. I can also produce a short shared-responsibility matrix for CC6/CC7 as you requested.

Two quick clarifications so we scope correctly:
1) When you say "carve-out subservice for AWS", are your auditors asking that Redwood's SOC 2 excludes the cloud provider (i.e., a carve-out) or that Redwood includes cloud controls via complementary user-entity controls (CUCs)? Either way we can document our reliance, but the artifact differs.
2) Do you need bridge letters (e.g., AWS bridge for audit gap coverage) or is a signed attestation from Redwood sufficient?

We have most of the artifacts ready; Karthik Iyer (cc'd) will pull the subprocessor CSV and the excerpted AWS SOC pages. I'll aim to get the package over by end-of-day Monday 2026-08-03.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Head, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Nimbus SOC 2 — what we can share and redaction guidance

Team —

Nimbus needs the dependency mapping and subprocessor evidence by 2026-08-04. I confirmed we can share Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report, plus excerpts from third-party (cloud) SOC reports and the subprocessor registry. Please follow the redaction rules below before dropping the files into the shared drive link: 

- Redact customer-identifying PII and any internal inventory IDs that are not meaningful to auditors.
- Keep control-text intact for CC6/CC7 excerpts — auditors need the control descriptions and testing results.
- Mark pages that reference our auditor's fieldwork dates (we'll include them in metadata).

Karthik — can you attach the latest subprocessor CSV and the AWS/GCP SOC excerpts? Marcus/Neha — confirm whether any vendor (e.g., managed DB vendor) had special carve-in coverage during the 2025 audit so we can flag them as in-scope.

I'll assemble the matrix (Redwood control -> cloud provider -> artifact filename) and produce a one-page attestation if a bridge letter from the cloud provider isn't available.

Thanks,
Irene

Attachment: action-items-nimbus-soc2.md

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Nimbus SOC 2 — what we can share and redaction guidance

Irene/Karthik —

Attached are the items pulled from the compliance vault: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (redacted per guidance), AWS_SOC_report_excerpt_2025.pdf (pages that reference infrastructure control testing), and subprocessor_registry_2026-07.csv. Notes:
- The 2025 audit treated AWS as a carve-out subservice for physical and infrastructure controls; our auditor performed complementary control testing for Redwood-managed logical access controls.
- GCP is used only for a small analytics pipeline; it was not in-scope for the 2025 SOC 2 Type II audit. We included the GCP artifact excerpt (none were in-scope) in the drive for transparency.
- The managed DB vendor (NimbusDBOps) was in-scope as a subprocessor during the 2025 audit and is flagged in the CSV (column: in_scope_for_2025_audit = TRUE).

I've uploaded the files to the Drive link and added a short mapping CSV (redwood_control_to_provider_map.csv). If Nimbus needs a provider bridge letter (e.g., from AWS) we can ask AWS risk/compliance, but historically customers accept our attestation plus the provider SOC excerpt.

Marcus Lin
Senior Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf, AWS_SOC_report_excerpt_2025.pdf, subprocessor_registry_2026-07.csv
